recipes.name: Easy Chicken and Broccoli Alfredo
ingredients_raw: 1 pound boneless skinless chicken breasts, cut into bite-sized pieces

steps.text: Cook pasta as directed on package, adding broccoli to the boiling water for the last 2 minutes of the pasta cooking time. Drain pasta mixture.
Meanwhile, heat dressing in large nonstick skillet on medium-high heat. Add chicken and cook until no longer pink in the center, stirring occasionally, about 5 to 7 minutes.
Stir in milk, cream cheese, Parmesan cheese, and basil. Bring to a boil, stirring constantly. Cook until sauce is well blended and heated through, about 1 to 2 minutes.
Add chicken mixture to pasta mixture; mix lightly.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Chicken and Broccoli Alfredo
raw_recipe.description: This creamy chicken and broccoli Alfredo pasta dish with fresh broccoli, tender chunks of chicken breast, Parmesan cheese, and basil is sure to please!

review.reviewBody: This recipes was great! My home smelled liked an Italian restaurant. I did, however, make a couple of changes. Instead of Italian Dressing, I used Good Seasons Italian Fat Free Salad Dressing Mix – 1.05oz, added 1/2 teaspoon of dried Parsley and 1/2 teaspoon of Garlic. I heated two tablespoons of Olive oil and sprinkled all of the seasonings on the chicken coating each side well. Once the chicken started to brown, I added the remaining ingredients. To compliment the dish, I served an Italian salad and homemade cheddar biscuits. Yum Yum!!

I doubled the Alfredo sauce part but only used the one pound of pasta as directed. I’m afraid I doctored it up quite a bit. Next time instead of cream cheese, I’ll use Boursin Garlic and Herb Cheese. I will add a teaspoon of salt as well as a teaspoon of pepper. I also added a teaspoon of garlic powder and I’ll use a teaspoon of onion powder as well. I probably added a tablespoon of Italian seasoning too. Last thing is I will probably not combine the pasta with the sauce. I’ll add the broccoli to the sauce however. Good basic recipe but I tweaked the dickens out of it. Thanks so much for the recipe ! I printed it out and wrote in my changes and additions.

Easy and tasty indeed! This is a great recipe for beginner cooks!! So glad the top line said your favorite pasta as I didn’t have any fettucine. I believe the dish could improve with the addition of fresh or garlic powder and a bit more broccoli. The biggest issue I had is with the Italian dressing overcooking and browning the bottom of the pan. I actually had to switch to another non-stick pan to finish cooking the chicken so it didn’t burn. Changes I made to this recipe: Used spaghetti instead of fettucine Used chicken tenders vs. chicken breast – quicker cooking time, less expensive and more tender Used heavy cream and 1% milk Added about ¼ cup of the pasta water and red pepper flakes

I just made this and it's the best Alfredo recipe I've ever had, considering I made a few changes. I gently cooked the chopped chicken tenderloins on the stove top with olive oil and covered them so they could steam and maintain moisture. When they were almost done I then added the Italian dressing to let them cook in that. The only other thing I did was used a little more Cream Cheese than required + added some parsley with the basil + chopped the broccoli very finely after boiling it with the EGG NOODLES I used. I also added 1 tablespoon of Lawrys seasoning salt and 1/2 tsp of garlic and onion powders. My family INHALED this delicious easy meal! Thank you!

WOW!!! So good AND easy! Had to make a few changes due to what was in the house. Angel hair ( 16 oz.) and no Italian dressing so ... put olive oil, cider vinegar, Italian seasoning, granulated garlic, and white pepper in the fry pan. Since the chicken breasts were 1.25# I upped the broccoli to 3 C, and the milk to 2 C. Kept everything else the same. Came out wonderful. Husband was going for seconds but decided he wanted it to last ( wants it again tomorrow!) Will definitely make this again, and again??. Thank you so much for posting this.

I find most of the sauces bland but this one was good, not overly delicious but good. I followed the advice of others and I reduced the milk to 1 cup and instead of using plain cream cheese, I used the Philadelphia cooking cream with garlic. I also added one diced zucchini to boost the amount of veggies in it.
I think the italian dressing gives the chicken a better taste that when added to the rest of the ingredients makes a good combination of flavours.

Delicious and easy recipe. I also added garlic, onion, salt/pepper and Italian seasoning when sautéing the chicken. And increased the cream cheese and parmesan cheese. Definitely a household favorite!

This recipe was good, I made it exactly following the recipe.
The next time I made it I left off the Italian dressing,instead I
Made a rioux with butter & flour, then added a cup of milk & stirred till it became thick & added the cream cheese & white pepper. Then poured the broccoli into the cream cheese sauce & added the Chicken(sometimes if in a hurry I use rotisserie
Chicken). Sprinkle with cheddar cheese. AndThen I take a tbsp or 2 of melted butter & a 1/2 cup to a one cup of breadcrumbs mix together & sprinkle over the casserole and bake. You don't need the pasta unless you want mor carbs. This makes a great
Pot luck dish, people love it.

This was really good. I added minced garlic and fresh mushrooms when cooking the chicken. The sauce looked a little thin, so just before adding the pasta and broccoli, I thickened it just a little bit with a cornstarch and milk mixture...don't need much though. Thanks for the recipe! I will be making this again.

My fiance and I really like this. I did add garlic and used frozen broccoli instead of fresh. Added a slurry (about 2 tsp cornstarch and 1/4 cup milk) to the chicken sauce to thicken it up. One surprising thing...chicken pieces still were a little on the bland side even though it was cooked in that salty italian dressing. My fiance made the suggestion of marinating the chicken in your choice of marinade before cooking. I think italian sausage will work well with this recipe too.

Mouthwatering! I did make some seasoning additions. I'm from the Deep South. I doubled the recipe and added a tablespoon of "Badia Louisiana Cajun Seasoning" to cover the chicken just before cooking it, 1 tablespoon minced garlic just before the chicken is done, and 1 teaspoon of "Kreative Kajun Kooking Magic Swamp Dust" seasoning before mixing the two parts together. Thanks for this delicious recipe
My husband loved it. I thought it would be better without the Italian dressing. I did sauté the chicken in butter so that helped too.
Very good. I did add Black pepper and garlic.
This recipe is the first one from the website and it was awesome. I cooked it at 11 years old and it was super easy to fallow. I highly recemend it
This came together so easily and I can't believe how creamy it was! I used shrimp in place of the chicken and my family loved it. I will be making this recipe again!

Chicken and broccoli Alfredo recipe is divine! It is very easy to make, and to save an extra step, I used a deep skillet that is similar to a walk. I was able to put the linguine and the brocco in it. then drained it and let it sit in my calendar while I use that same skillet to cook my chicken in the sauce. The sauce looks like it’s runny while you’re cooking it, but once it mixes in with the linguine, just melds together into this wonderful sauce. it is absolutely wonderful! Love it!
My grandson helped me make this and it was good. I agree the sauce is thin but I was ok with that. It was really good for a quick dinner and I actually had all the ingredients.
It’s OK. It needs to be creamier. I would season chicken when cooking as others suggested and would add garlic or other desired seasoning because it was a little bland.

The flavor comes out OK but there are a few things here that really dont work. Using milk instead of cream results in a really thin sauce. Also using italian dressing as a marinade for the chicken can really overpower the flavor of the dish. So just expect that and if that is your flavor preference this works. Also make sure to at least do some simple season(salt & pepper) to the chicken before you cook it and brine it for a few minutes if you really want juicier chicken.
I'm not a big fan of pasta....But this one was okay
